text:
maria: Heads-up — prod decrypt failures right after CMK rotation. Our service (acct 987654321098) assumes role into acct 123456789012 and fails on envelope decrypt with AccessDenied. App log: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/session is not authorized to use kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789`
jamal: Oof. Did you check the key policy vs the assumed-role ARN? after rotation the key-policy might have been narrowed to `Principal: { AWS: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/KMSInvoker" }` and not include the cross-account principal.
alex: Also confirm whether the caller is an assumed-role principal or an STS session principal. Key policies that whitelist `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role` won't match `arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/session` unless you allowed the role (not the assumed session) or used `"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role"`.
olivia: Another common gotcha: session policies can remove `kms:Decrypt` even if role has it. Can you paste the role's inline policies + any session policy?
maria: Minimal snippets below. Role inline policy includes `"Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "*"`. Key policy on rotated key has a condition `"aws:SourceAccount": "123456789012"` and principal set to `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role`. CloudTrail event shows `userIdentity.type = AssumedRole` and `userIdentity.arn = arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/Session`.
jamal: If the key policy uses `aws:SourceAccount` condition it should be fine, but SourceAccount only checks the account of the caller, not the STS ARN format. If key policy is restricting by exact principal, you need to include the `arn:aws:sts::*:assumed-role/...` pattern or allow the IAM role principal (not the session). Example safe principal in key policy: `"Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role" }`.
alex: Also check for missing `kms:Decrypt` on the KMS Grant if you're relying on grants rather than key policy. Grants are ephemeral and tied to specific granteePrincipal ARNs; rotation may have invalidated old grants. Run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` and see if a grant exists for the role.
maria: Ran list-grants — empty. We do use grants in older code paths for envelope reuse; rotation job deleted and recreated the key so previous grants are gone.
olivia: That explains it. If you relied on a grant created in acct 123... to let acct 987... decrypt, grants don't survive key replacements. Need to either recreate grant for the new key or rely on key policy + role permissions.
j amal: Quick remediation options: 1) add vault key policy allowing `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role` (or the sts assumed-role pattern) with `kms:Decrypt`; 2) recreate cross-account grant with `GranteePrincipal` set to `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role` (note grants are created in the CMK account); 3) if you want shortest blast radius, add a grant token workflow during rollout.
alex: If you go with policy, example snippet: `"Statement": [{ "Sid": "AllowCrossAccountAssumeRole", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-app-role" }, "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": "*" }]` — and keep SourceAccount condition if helpful.
maria: Thanks. For long-term we should stop relying on grants for cross-account decrypts. They make rotation and auditing harder.
sec-bot: CloudTrail alert — 1843205625: KMSDecryptDenied for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789 from principal arn:aws:sts::987654321098:assumed-role/redwood-app-role/Session. Detected after CMK rotation job at 1843201000.
deploy-bot: FYI: rotation job 2026-11-20T02:30Z rolled new key and updated aliases; automated grant recreation disabled by feature flag.
olivia: Action items: (1) Add a temporary key policy entry to allow the role (maria to submit PR), (2) Recreate necessary cross-account grants if any services still use them (jamal), (3) Plan removing grant-based flow and switch to stable key-policy permissions (olivia + sec).
maria: Will open PR in a few mins with the policy change, will include audit rationale and TTL for the temp allow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
